A_target.statement:
Let $p: Y \to X$ be a [[Definition:Regular Covering|regular covering map]] with $Y$ [[Definition:Connected Space|connected]] and [[Definition:Locally Path-Connected Space|locally path-connected]].
Then:
:$X \cong Y / \map {\operatorname {Deck} } p$
where $\map {\operatorname {Deck} } p$ is the [[Definition:Deck Transformation|group of deck transformations]].

B_source.statement:
Let a [[Definition:Group|group]] $G$ act [[Definition:Free Group Action|freely]] and [[Definition:Properly Discontinuous Group Action|properly discontinuously]] on a space $Y$.
Then the [[Definition:Quotient Mapping|quotient map]] $Y \to Y / G$ onto the [[Definition:Orbit Space|orbit space]] is a [[Definition:Covering Map|covering map]].

substitutions.the group acting on the space: the deck transformation group of the covering
substitutions.the orbits of the action: the fibres of the covering map
substitutions.the orbit space: the base space of the covering

derived.freeness of the action: no nonidentity deck transformation fixes a point, which holds by uniqueness of lifts

validity_conditions: The deck group acts freely because a deck transformation fixing a point agrees with the identity on a lift and hence everywhere, by uniqueness of lifts.
The action is properly discontinuous because evenly covered neighbourhoods separate the sheets, giving each point a neighbourhood moved off itself by every nonidentity element.

Regularity of the covering is what makes the deck group act transitively on each fibre, so that the orbits are exactly the fibres; for a nonregular covering the orbit space is a proper quotient of the base.
proof_plan:
Let $\phi \in \map {\operatorname {Deck} } p$ with $\map \phi y = y$ for some $y$.
By [[Uniqueness of Lifts]], $\phi = \operatorname {id}_Y$.
Hence the action is [[Definition:Free Group Action|free]].

Let $U \subseteq X$ be [[Definition:Evenly Covered|evenly covered]], and $V$ a sheet over $U$.
Distinct deck transformations permute the sheets, so $\map \phi V \cap V = \O$ for $\phi \ne \operatorname {id}$.
Hence the action is [[Definition:Properly Discontinuous Group Action|properly discontinuous]].

As $p$ is [[Definition:Regular Covering|regular]], $\map {\operatorname {Deck} } p$ acts [[Definition:Transitive Group Action|transitively]] on each fibre $\map {p^{-1} } x$.
Hence the orbits are exactly the fibres of $p$.

Thus $p$ induces a continuous bijection $Y / \map {\operatorname {Deck} } p \to X$, which is a [[Definition:Homeomorphism|homeomorphism]] as both quotient maps are [[Definition:Open Mapping|open]].
{{qed}}
